description:
🇧🇷 PACIFICADORES 🐢🚀

We are the Pacificadores, a team ready to explore the unknown, protect our planet, and uncover the stories left behind in space!

Just like the Ninja Turtles, we work together, each bringing our own strengths to the team. Our mission is to bring forgotten NASA equipment back into the spotlight.

From the Moon to Mars, no piece of history deserves to be forgotten. After all, even heroes leave their mark on the universe! 🌎🌕🔴
summary:
Echoes of Astra is a browser-based visual novel for the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars." The player, grandchild of retired enginer Tadeu, starts out calling his keepsakes "old junk." Putting on Tadeu's old helmet powers up ECO, the AI ​​inside the visor. ECO picks up faint signals from four pieces of hardware NASA left behind: the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, the three Lunar Roving Vehicles from Apollo 15 to 17, the Spirit rover stuck in Gusev Crater, and the Phoenix lander on the Martian arctic plains.

ECO guides the player to each machine and briefs them on their personality. Every meeting is a conversation, and the player has to respond with respect. Treating Eagle like a celebrity or calling Spirit a failure cuts the signal, and ECO ends the event. Choosing well unlocks the machine's real history and a collectible based on a real object, such as the Tranquility Base Plaque, for the Memories collection.

The game teaches history through empathy, and every date and fact comes from one lore reference file. It presents discarded equipment as heritage that stays alive while someone keeps telling its story.
details:
Echoes of Astra: Project Details

What it does and how it works

Echoes of Astra is a visual novel that runs in a web browser. The player enters a name and starts in the attic of Grandpa Tadeu, a retired astronaut. When the player puts on his old helmet, ECO, the AI inside the visor, switches on. ECO detects signals from four pieces of hardware NASA left behind: the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage and the Lunar Roving Vehicles on the Moon, and the Spirit rover and Phoenix lander on Mars.

The player picks a destination and then a machine. ECO describes the machine's personality, and the conversation begins. Each stage has three choices, and only answers that respect the machine move the story forward. A careless answer makes the machine shut down, ECO reports the signal as lost, and the player tries the stage again.

After three good answers, the machine tells its real history and gives the player an item based on a real object or discovery. The item goes into the Memories collection. After all four stages, the player returns to the attic and tells Grandpa what they learned. Progress saves automatically, so players can stop and continue later.

Benefits

It runs in any modern browser and needs no install, account or server.

Each stage is short: one conversation with three choices. That fits a classroom or a quick break.

Players learn real facts in context. For example, Spirit tells them it was built for about 90 days and kept going for over six years.

Mistakes cost little. The machine's reaction shows what went wrong, and the player tries again.

No personal data leaves the device. Saves stay in the browser.

Intended impact

We want players to see discarded spacecraft as heritage instead of scrap. This matters most for younger people, who weren't alive for Apollo or Spirit. The protagonist starts out calling the hardware "old junk" and ends up wanting to share the stories "at school, online, everywhere." We hope players do the same. The game also practices a skill that goes beyond space history: working out how someone wants to be treated and responding with respect.

Tools and technologies
Language: TypeScript (strict mode)

Framework and build: React 19, Vite 8

Interface: HeroUI and Tailwind CSS 4, with Framer Motion for scene transitions, character entrances and typewriter text
State and saves: Zustand, with a versioned save system stored in the browser's localStorage

Audio: Howler.js, which changes the music automatically for each scene

Fonts: Inter, Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (Google Fonts)

Development: VS Code, Cursor and Kiro (AI coding assistants), ESLint, Git and GitHub

Hardware: none beyond ordinary computers, for building or for playing

How it is creative

Personalities come from real history. Eagle is solemn because it carried the first crewed landing. It says "I was not left behind. I stayed," because its descent stage was the launchpad for the crew's return. The LRVs are playful buggies who joke about flying to the Moon folded up "like a piece of origami." Spirit is sleepy and poetic because it fell silent in the Martian winter, stuck in sand. Phoenix is a science geek who explains how it baked soil in tiny ovens to "sniff" the gases.

Empathy is the puzzle. Players don't solve item puzzles or need fast reflexes. They progress by understanding a character.

Failure is a lost signal. A game over looks like the way real missions end.
Every reward is real. The items are the Tranquility Base Plaque, the Genesis Rock, Big Muley and Orange Soil, the silica soil Spirit found at Home Plate, and Phoenix's confirmation of water ice.

The interface changes with the world. The colors are solar orange on the ship, cyan on the Moon and oxide red on Mars, in a style based on NASA telemetry screens.
The frame story uses imagination. A grandfather hands over his helmet and says, "Use your imagination as your spaceship."

Factors the team considered

Historical accuracy: All dates, names and technical details come from one reference file, and the team has a rule against inventing facts. Where history is uncertain, the game says so. For example, no one has confirmed where Eagle's ascent stage crashed.

Tone: The challenge says "abandoned but not forgotten," so the game rejects pity as firmly as it rejects contempt. Feeling sorry for a machine counts as a wrong answer.

No generative AI during play: All dialogue is written in advance and fact-checked, and every player sees the same lines. ECO is a scripted character, not a live AI.

Readability and comfort: Dialogue lines are short, the typewriter text can be skipped, and the item reward animation follows the device's reduced-motion setting.

Resilience: If an image or audio file is missing, the game shows a placeholder or plays silence instead of breaking.

Maintainability: The story is stored as typed data, separate from the interface code, so writers can edit dialogue without changing any components.
